experiment: 15N R1, R1rho (converted to R2) and 1H-15N NOE at 800 MHz
buffer: 20 mM sodium phosphate, 100 mM NaCl, 0.01% NaN3
other_conditions: 2 mM 13C,15N-AcrIIA4 (NMR sample); tumbling: tau_c = 6.2 ns; regime (authors): ps-ns motions in the beta1-beta2 loop and us-ms conformational exchange in other loops; related structures: 5XN4 (free solution structure, this paper)
timescale: ps-ns (beta1-beta2 loop G21-I27, NOE below 0.8) and us-ms exchange (T22, N23, S26, N48, S50, G62, E68; from elevated R2); no model-free fit
alt_state_structure: 5VW1: AcrIIA4 bound to SpyCas9-sgRNA, beta1-beta2 loop without regular secondary structure versus the 3(10) helix T22-N25 in free solution (Results, Figure 1C,D; Figure 3A)
author_claim: Secondary structure is rigid (NOE above 0.8) while the Cas9-binding loops are dynamic: beta1-beta2 loop on ps-ns and us-ms, beta3-alpha2 and alpha2-alpha3 loops on us-ms.
anchor: In addition, increased 15 N R 2 relaxation rates indicated the presence of slower conformational exchanges in μs‒ms timescales in the β1–β2 loop (Thr22, Asn23, and Ser26), the β3–α2 loop (Asn48 and Ser50) and the α2–α3 loop (Gly62 and Glu68) regions.
locator: Results, Backbone dynamics reveals characteristic motions at the binding interface (Figure 2, Figure 3B); conditions: Methods, NMR spectroscopy
caveat_note: Deposit card has no BMRB sample entry; temperature (25 °C = 298 K) and field (800 MHz) match the sheet values. Residues S20, S24, T28, Q29, E47, Q65 are completely broadened (exchange), not measured. Other Cas9 complex crystal structures are cited by number only.

experiment: 1H-15N HSQC titration of 15N-AcrIIA4 with unlabeled apo SpyCas9, intensity ratio I_bound/I_free at 10% bound
ligand_or_partner: apo SpyCas9 (0.02 mM Cas9 with 0.2 mM AcrIIA4; also tested at 10 °C and 45 °C)
other_conditions: 10% bound titration point; regime (authors): intermediate exchange; related structures: 5VW1
author_claim: Binding to the 158.4 kDa SpyCas9 broadens nearly all AcrIIA4 amides without chemical-shift changes, caused by complex size and by intermediate exchange; interface residues Y67 and D69 broaden most.
anchor: This indicates that the line broadening is caused not only by the large complex formation, but also by intermediate exchange from the interaction.
caveat_note: Line broadening mixes the slow tumbling of the large complex with intermediate exchange, and the authors could not separate them or map the interface. Titration buffer and pH are not stated separately; the ITC buffer included 5 mM BME. N87 is the only residue still visible at 1:1.
